html:
The Dorset culture was a Paleo-Inuit people who lived across the Canadian Arctic and Greenland from about 500 BCE until about 1300 CE. It is named after Cape Dorset on Baffin Island, where its remains were first identified.

The Dorset hunted seals and walrus from the ice and built snow houses and stone longhouses, but they seem not to have used bows, dogs or kayaks like later peoples. They carved small, striking figures of animals and humans in ivory and wood.

They vanished as the Thule, ancestors of the Inuit, spread east from Alaska after 1000 CE. Inuit stories tell of the Tuniit, strong but shy people who lived in the land before them. The Dorset may have met the Norse too.
